beliefs.practice: Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection URI only in an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) and never commit it; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead of the real secret.

Create a single MongoClient/connection instance at app startup and reuse it everywhere (do not open a new connection per request); set an appropriate maxPoolSize (e.g., maxPoolSize=50) in the connection options.
Enable TLS/SSL on the connection (ssl=true / tls=true) and verify certificates; do not disable TLS in production or log connection strings with tls flags turned off.
Prefer managed identity / Azure AD or short-lived credentials to long-lived account keys when possible; avoid baking primary keys into app configuration or source control.
Restrict cluster access with network controls: use IP firewall rules and/or VNet service endpoints/private link so only the app host(s) can reach the DocumentDB cluster.

When loading or seeding many documents, use bulk writes (insertMany with ordered:false or bulkWrite) and tune writeConcern (e.g., { w:1 }) to improve throughput and to make seeding idempotent use upsert or unique eventId keys.

Create a compound index to support the common timeline query pattern, e.g., { customerId: 1, timestamp: 1 } (and include channel as a second or covered field if you filter/sort by it) so per-customer sorting by timestamp is index-backed.

For aggregation pipelines, put $match and $sort stages as early as possible and ensure the sort fields are covered by an index; prefer pipelines like [{$match: {...}}, {$sort: {timestamp:1}}, {$group: {...}}].
Use projection to return only required fields (e.g., { timestamp:1, channel:1, eventType:1, metadata:1 }) to reduce RU consumption and network transfer in both aggregation and find queries.
Validate index usage with explain() (executionStats) for representative aggregation pipelines and tune indexes or pipeline shape until the explain shows index scans rather than COLLSCAN.

Build vector indexes only on a dedicated vector field with a fixed dimensionality and explicit index parameters (e.g., index type HNSW with specific M and efConstruction or DiskANN parameters) and ensure the index creation script is idempotent.
Normalize or fix vector dimensionality and, if using cosine similarity, normalize vectors (unit length) at insert time so vector comparisons are consistent and the index behaves correctly.

When combining metadata filters with vector search, pre-filter by metadata (e.g., $match customerId and channel) and then run the vector search on the smaller set (hybrid filtering) to reduce RU cost and improve latency.
Implement exponential backoff retries on transient errors (network failures, timeouts) and explicitly handle 429/RU-throttling responses by reading Retry-After headers and retrying after that delay.

Plan throughput: monitor RU/s consumption for typical aggregations and provision/scale throughput (or use autoscale) so heavy aggregations or vector searches are not throttled during normal operation.

Avoid unbounded memory operations in aggregation ($group that builds huge arrays); instead stream results, page by timestamp range, or use $limit and incremental aggregation to keep working set bounded.
Create unique indexes for idempotency (e.g., unique index on eventId) so seed scripts can upsert or ignore duplicates safely when re-run.
Use allowDiskUse: true for aggregation pipelines that require large sorts or groupings so queries can spill to disk instead of failing or using excessive memory, and measure RU impact.

Use cursor.batchSize and server-side cursors for large result sets and avoid skip-based pagination for timelines; prefer range-based pagination on timestamp (e.g., timestamp > lastSeen) to keep performance predictable.
Instrument and monitor: collect metrics for RU consumption, latency, index usage, connection pool utilization and 429s; use those metrics to adjust indexes, queries and throughput.

Make index creation idempotent in startup/infra scripts (use createIndexes with the exact same specification) and avoid creating indexes on very large collections during peak production traffic without scheduling maintenance.

Avoid large $lookup or cross-collection joins in pipelines for per-customer timelines; denormalize frequently-read event metadata into the event document to make the timeline aggregation simpler and indexable.
Protect secrets and telemetry: never log the full connection string or primary keys; mask or omit secrets in error messages and telemetry sent to logs or APM.

If the MongoDB wire protocol version or features (retryable writes, transactions) are needed, verify the cluster wire version and supported features before using them; do not assume full MongoDB parity.
Add TTL indexes on ephemeral event collections (e.g., session traces) to reclaim storage automatically (createIndex({ createdAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: N })) where appropriate.
